picked.t: 5 Vietnamese restaurants named among Asia-Pacific's 100 best by Tatler
picked.body: Anan Saigon, Upstairs Tasting Room, Nephele, and CieL Dining in Ho Chi Minh City joined Hanoi's Gia on the list that was unveiled in Shanghai last month. The selection brings together restaurants offering different interpretations of Vietnamese cooking and menus drawing on European and other Asian influences. Set within a market, Anan Saigon offers chef Peter Cuong Franklin's creative takes on familiar Vietnamese dishes, from tacos inspired by banh xeo , the country's crispy savory pancakes, to fish sauce ice cream. Vietnamese flavors also shape the 12-course tasting menu at Upstairs Tasting Room, led by chef Hiep Truong. His dishes range from wagyu beef salad with small eggplants and herbs to charcoal-grilled duck inspired by a traditional Hue recipe from central Vietnam. At Nephele, a renovated historic building provides the setting for a single dinner tasting menu with Vietnamese influences. The meal unfolds across the property, beginning on the ground floor and continuing upstairs in the main dining room before ending with small sweets at the bar as vinyl records play, according to the Michelin Guide. In Thao Dien area, home to HCMC's largest expat community, CieL Dining brings European and Asian influences together in a minimalist dining room with an open kitchen. Brittany oysters are paired with sparkling wine and green apple, while herbs grown at the restaurant find their way into its dishes. Hanoi representative Gia explores Vietnamese culinary traditions through a seasonal tasting menu centered on local ingredients. Its setting on Van Mieu Street echoes the connection to heritage, with interiors inspired by the nearby Temple of Literature. Four of the five, Anan Saigon, Upstairs, CieL, and Gia, have one Michelin star in the 2026 selection. Upstairs earned its first star this year. Tatler covers dining, travel, fashion, and culture, and its annual Tatler Best awards recognize restaurants, hotels, and bars across the Asia-Pacific. Winners are selected through editorial nominations and evaluations by hospitality professionals, critics, journalists, and experienced travelers.

picked.t: Thai women rank third among foreign brides of South Korean men
picked.body: About 1,400 Thai women married South Korean men last year, out of 15,300 foreign brides, Yonhap reported Thursday, citing data from South Korea's Data and Statistics Ministry. Vietnamese women topped the list with 25.3%, followed by Chinese women at 15.1%. South Korea registered 21,399 multicultural marriages in 2025, including those between South Korean women and foreign men, a slight decline of 0.2% from the previous year, according to the Bangkok Post. Marriages between South Korean men and foreign women accounted for 71.4% of all multicultural unions, while those involving foreign husbands made up 18.9%. The remaining 9.7% involved naturalized South Korean citizens. The average age at first marriage was 37.1 years for husbands and 29.7 years for wives. Husbands were older than their wives in 75.2% of multicultural marriages, with an age gap of at least 10 years in 36.1% of all such unions.

picked.t: Homicide squad takes over hunt for 13-year-old Vietnamese girl missing in Berlin
picked.body: Lisa Ta left her family's home on Golliner Strasse in the eastern Berlin district of Marzahn at around 7:20 a.m. that day, according to police. She was due to set off from Barnimplatz for her school on Sella-Hasse-Strasse 10 minutes later but never arrived. Police and the Berlin prosecutor's office announced on Friday that the 5th homicide squad of the State Criminal Police Office (LKA) had taken over, saying in a joint statement that investigators currently assume Lisa did not leave home voluntarily. The LKA's missing persons unit had been handling the case until then, Berliner Zeitung reported. "There is an initial suspicion of a criminal offense," a spokesperson for the prosecutor's office told the German Press Agency ( dpa ), declining to give further details. Police launched a large-scale search on Friday, deploying sniffer dogs as a helicopter flew over the area's prefabricated apartment blocks and green spaces, the agency reported. Officers were back on site on Saturday morning as the search resumed, prosecutor's office spokesperson Michael Petzold said. Berlin daily Tagesspiegel noted that the LKA division housing the city's eight homicide squads investigates not only suspected killings but also suspected kidnappings and abductions for ransom. Police describe Lisa as about 160-165 cm tall and slim, with long dark hair. She was last seen wearing a black quilted jacket with a hood, blue flared jeans and white-beige DC sneakers, and carrying a black backpack with no brand logo. Police, who released her photos on the day she disappeared, are asking anyone who saw her after 7:15 a.m. on Tuesday, knows where she is or has been in contact with her since to come forward. Tips can be given to the homicide squad at +49 30 4664-911555 or at any police station. Lisa's mother, Nguyen Hoai Xoan, asked friends and the Vietnamese community in Berlin and across Germany on Thursday to print missing-person notices and put them up on their doors or at the entrances to apartment buildings, TamdaMedia , a Vietnamese-language news site in Europe, reported. "For now, the police have no new information either. The family is truly on tenterhooks and only hopes everyone will lend a hand so she can be found soon," she said.
